Ravensburger Krypt Gold 631 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults - 15152 - Every Piece is Unique, Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly This was my first puzzle of this brand. While the pieces did fit together well, I noticed several pieces that out of the box had pegs that were bent, or paper lifting. While it didnt interfere with the puzzle assembly it just made the completed puzzle look ragged.

I suggest labeling the puzzle map to orient a "top" or "bottom" as during assembly you may accidently turn your map upside down.

Organizing the pieces is what I found most helpful by size, shape, and if has a curve/turn or not. Then when you reach a portion of the puzzle that you need, you can brute force from your pile.

Several pieces are very unique, and thus can serve as anchors to build off of.

The hardest part is the border, something I usually do first, as the pieces do not interlock on the edges, you have to do another layer in in order to interlock the edge pieces. Once I put the pieces in piles of similar size/shape, the puzzle assembly speed went much faster.

Took me about 20-25 hours total.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Krypt Gold 631 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults - 15152 - Every Piece is Unique, Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly

This vanilla option is much better. In anticipation of less than ideal taste I added some good quality vanilla extract which also helped boost the flavor.

Still, the issues I had with the chocolate version are also present in this version. The box it comes in is cheap and flimsy, and dented up quite a bit in transit. It makes for a poor presentation should this be a gift item. On the plus side, the sprinkle packet stayed closed in the vanilla kit box (it broke open in the chocolate kit box and there were sprinkles everywhere). The frosting packet is inside the main pouch with loose flour, so it's a messy proposition to get the frosting packet out -- flour spills easily. Lastly, the silicone molds are quite flimsy. Putting them into something supportive, such as a muffin tin, is highly recommended prior to filling and baking.

The vanilla donuts have a much better flavor than the chocolate, especially when additional vanilla extract is added. The assembly process is simple and, while kids will need supervision (especially when dealing with the silicone molds) it's a fun activity.

Taking all the pros and cons into consideration puts my score at 3.5 stars. It's a great idea, but some of the kinks need to be ironed out to make it a kit that is worth the price charged.
text_fidelity_b: PLANET BAKE Vegan Donut Making Kit - Plant-Based, Gluten Free Donut Kit with Pre-Measured Ingredients & Silicone Donut Molds - Complete Kids Baking Set for Ages 4-12 (Vanilla)

text_fidelity_a:
Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor [[VIDEOID:c9ed210fcea7bd15ff238268da66c6e5]] I really liked this classic game of Sorry. I hadn't played this game in over 25 years, so this is a fun blast from the past.

The game isn't as silly or as random as I remember it. For a random move your pawn game, there is actually a decent amount of strategy involved.

The rules were a bit confusing, since they used the old 1959 rules. Here's my summary of the rules: You can only move your pawns out of start if you pick a 1, 2, or sometimes a Sorry card. If you get a 1 or a 2, then you only move out to the first circle. You only slide when you get on the first part of the slide. If you can't move, you don't move, and you need an exact count to get into the Home square. Follow the rest of the instructions on the cards.

Pros:
+It's possible to win no matter how far behind a player is
+Great rendition of a classic game
+A lot of fun
+Great for any ages

Cons:
-The rules are a bit confusing. I had to clarify some of the rules on the internet.
-The game starts out very slowly
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor

text_fidelity_a:
FurReal Friends Pax My Poopin Pup Plush Toy (Amazon Exclusive) I had high hopes for this little pooping doggo.. I purchased as a Christmas gift for my daughter (3 years old), who was obsessed with walking our dog and watching him pop (she’s a weirdo). Overall, she has gotten a fair amount of play and enjoyment out of the little fella, so I would *probably* purchase again.

Pros: He makes cute little doggy noises, he’s has soft fur.

Cons: He was much smaller than I expected (but my fault, as size is objective). He was overall much harder than I expected (other than his thin layer of fuzzy fur coat, he’s completely hard to the squeeze). He has wheels (which for some reason I thought he was more automatic than that). The leash is short (it was the perfect size for my tiny 3 year old when we bought it, but our 4 year old friend had to bend over to push it around). The treats / poo pellets are incredibly small. We lost a couple on christmas when we opened the gift.. and then a few more since. We have less than half left now (which I think is an accomplishment since we’ve had it almost a year!).

My toddler and her friends have enjoyed playing with it, but they have 1) been hurt by his hard material build (just minor boo boo, but still) 2) tried to eat the teeny pellet foods (cause, why not?) and 3) shoved other objects in its mouth that they weren’t supposed to. The design concept isn’t bad, but I do wish it was slightly bigger, with slightly bigger treats, a slightly longer leash, slightly more “squeezable”... you catch my drift. And with all that in mind, I probably would have gone with a different puppers.
text_fidelity_b: FurReal Friends Pax My Poopin Pup Plush Toy (Amazon Exclusive)

SmartLab Toys Squishy Human Body with 21 Removable Body Parts with Anatomy Book This product has the potential to be an incredible teaching tool which is why I initially purchased it. However, it is evident after ordering this item (even after a replacement of the original product that was initially delivered--replacement is shown in pictures above), that there are reoccurring issues with this item that are extremely problematic.

You can see how there are pieces of this product that come lodged incorrectly including the skull which does not stay in its designated hole. The large intestine looks like it's already been pulled apart by a child passed its point of stretch as it is extremely thin at the connection area.

Also--I if I as a teacher could not even put this item in full back together, I can only imagine how difficult this would be for a child of any age to maneuver as well.

If this company would just give more effort into putting out a quality product it would be extremely useful across-the-board and save them so much money in returns if they would just take the small effort to fix these ongoing issues that so many purchasers report.

I was able to get a 25% refund on my initial purchase with being able to keep the item as I explained I do not want to do a third replacement bit instead that I would rather just find a innovative way to make the issues I've experienced usable for teaching my students.

If you get this product don't settle for a poor quality item...they used to be made so well and now this company has made cheaply made pieces of it the regular. Stick to your guns on insisting on either a working product and/or a refund.

Wish you all the best with this item.

They pretend they are firefighters/paramedics/doctors constantly, and LOVE watching the old show "Emergency". They also enjoy Bubble Guppies occasionally, so when I saw this check-up center, I guessed that they would enjoy it.

I guessed correctly! They fell in love with it.

Unfortunately, they caught sight of the "Clambulance" on the back of the box(and all the other items that *didn't* come in this set, and it took a moment to curb their disappointment. Overall, if you get this check-up center, I do recommend getting at least a couple of the other characters to go with it, along with at least the "clambulance" or helicopter. And I like having crafts like this where they can sit indoors and make things that they can give away as a gift, or they can use it themselves.
With this MeJoji kit, they can make 5 bracelets and necklaces. They come up with their own designs so it makes them unique to who they are.
The older kids help the younger ones trace and color a design using the included pencils. I then take the colored pieces and put them into the oven so harden them up and shrink them. I did have some beads, from some other kit we had, and added those to the cord. Just something to fill in the space and to add a lot more color.

text_fidelity_a:
Holy Stone HS270 GPS 2.7K Drone with FHD FPV Camera Live Video for Adults, Portable Selfie Quadcopter with 2 Batteries for Beginners with Auto Return Home, Custom Flight Path, Follow Me, Auto Hover [[VIDEOID:bf921d7e8b73b1b75b44b485dab75323]] So after a week of having this unit I had 9 flights and was pleased to fly it! Although I had an issue once don't know if that was just the bird or that was me, I'm leaning toward me as I might have not turned the drone in the right direction and had a failure to calibrate or that could been just the area I was in and its inability to gain GPS, with that said it was pretty much a problem free week of flying the 270. Now dealing with the single battery was an issue, I do think they should offer a package or drone deal with 2 batteries standard. 😁.

I will say it is a great beginner drone for young teens are adults that want to get into flying. From the moment I unboxed it it felt great in my hands it didn't feel cheap most of the construction was plastic but with that said it is very consistent with some of the quality that I've become accustomed to with the hs700 the hs190 and a hs720. The controller is smaller then what I'm used to. It felt good in the hand but a lil small for my liking as I used my Galaxy Note 9 which is the limit as far as the holder, every other feature like the FPV, follow me mode and plotting way points , and circle point of interest on a map and it's going there and coming back worked pretty well. The Return too home when low on Battery functioned well as I flew the bird too that point almost everytime, there was an issue with the follow me I should have had it up a little higher it did hit a branch on a tree which was my fault because these drones do not come with obstacle avoidance and it took a fall to the ground no worse for wear I stopped the motors flipped back over unlock the motors and she went right back up no issues. Photo quality really really love the camera and take some great pictures even out that 400 ft. I really like the 4K camera and the quality of the video and pictures ( all photos post are unedited) and this unit also allows you to record record audio which is pretty good for bloggers , though my one gripe is I wish the 270 came with a gimbal to really make exceptional video, but at this price point it's a trade off!

The HS270 is very very wind resistant I flew this in pretty high winds somewhere between 15 to maybe 18 miles an hour and some strong gusts I thought for sure it going to blow over the pond or even into some of the trees. The GPS worked awesome as it kept the unit in its place and even though in my video it was shaky because you could see the wind is blowing it all over the place I was thoroughly impressed and this bird should not fly away from you unless you accidentally turn off the GPS in which case you really need to know how to fly this thing or any drones in the wind with the GPS off. It has a 3-speed future from low medium to high I enjoyed that it seemed like when it was windy I kicked it in high speed and it flew alot better keeping in medium most of the other times I enjoy a quick flights back and forth but was able to enjoy the roughly 21 minutes of flying time at the most and less on that really windy day it was only about 16 minutes most of the time it was fighting the wind. It takes pretty good pictures fpv to the cell phone like 720pvideo and 2K photo But the quality really comes to life when you have a SD card in the unit.

I think overall this unit does exactly as it's advertised to do and being able to fold up you can actually take this thing with you on vacation put in your suitcase carry out with you when you go on a hike and have something with you besides your camera that you can put up into the air and taking it up sectional a different view all of your vacation or a picture of you and your family or significant other standing by a Mountain or even the Grand Canyon with a drone from a distance and capture something that cant be done with a selfie stick. So I recommend this unit, but make sure you get extra batteries cuz it does take a while with the USB plug to charge the battery, most times it took 2-3 hours till fully charged. I grabbed a case on Amazon which I believe it was a case setup for a DJI mavic I did a little modifying on the sides of the hard foam and it was able to sit down in the case well which I showed the picture in the reviews it was the soyan case for like 22 bucks or something like that. All in all a great deal, I'm totally satisfied!
text_fidelity_b: Holy Stone HS270 GPS 2.7K Drone with FHD FPV Camera Live Video for Adults, Portable Selfie Quadcopter with 2 Batteries for Beginners with Auto Return Home, Custom Flight Path, Follow Me, Auto Hover

text_fidelity_a: Chompin' Charlie Game - Feed The Squirrel Acorns And Race To Collect Them When They Scatter - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath This is a perfect addition to the Fall basket. There are always lots of books about squirrels and acorns to add to the fall line-up and this game goes with them well. It's a great companion to those books and we've all had fun with it. There's also a little puzzle to go with the game, which adds more fun to the squirrel/acorn focus. To play the game, the players take turns rolling a die. The color/number that is rolled is what color and how many(up to 2) acorns you put into Charlie's mouth. Once he gets full, the acorns roll out the holes that are in the tree trunk that Charlie stands on. Using only one hand, the players race to collect the acorns. The first player to fill up their acorn stash card wins. The rules say that if a player rolls a certain color and it's not in the main stash of acorns, that player has to take one of their collected acorns or take one from another player. Taking from another player won't be for all families, but it can be adapted, if desired. Also, with the acorns rolling everywhere, it's tricky finding the best place to play. The acorns will roll off the table, but if on the floor, they could roll under things, like couches, if it's a smaller space. Our home is small, so we try to put up little "walls" to make sure the acorns don't roll under things. Overall, it's a fun game and the quality of it is nice, too. It's a simple game that's a great way to add a bit of joy to a day.
text_fidelity_b: Chompin' Charlie Game - Feed The Squirrel Acorns And Race To Collect Them When They Scatter - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath

Easy Bake Ultimate Oven, Pink/Purple I got the Easy Bake Ultimate Oven for my little boy. What woman doesn't love it when a man can cook?! ;) He's almost 3, so not quite the targeted age, but we still had fun with it.

What we like:
-I like that it's purple, which is a LITTLE bit more on the neutral side.
-It cooks very quickly. You preheat for 20 minutes and then cook an average of 10 minutes or so. You get exact directions, though. I was expecting a MUCH longer cook time.

What we didn't like:
-You can't watch the food while it cooks. I wish the front was clear, and it would have made this a much better learning tool, and made it a lot more fun.
-The portions are TINY! Seriously, I don't think it would fill up a mouse! But, I guess I have to expect tiny portions for it to cook so quickly. And, I think it's more of a "time together" kind of activity!

Just some neutral information we learned. You can cook "regular" food in the oven. If you're like us, you can't pay a lot of money for tiny mixes that produce 1/10th of the size of a normal cookie. Just save a little batter from when you cook. I also learned that you CAN burn food in this oven. :) So make sure you set a timer.
The pictures in the directions have cute, perfect little cookies and cupcakes. Ours didn't even come close to looking that great. Maybe with a little more practice?!
This oven comes with a batch of cookies and cupcakes w/frosting, sugar crystals, and cupcake wraps. It also has two cooking pans and an "arm" to push the pans into the oven. It has spots marked to make sure you get them to the correct spot to cook and cool. Overall, we've had a lot of fun with it!

And this is probably obvious, but it's electric. ;)
text_fidelity_b: Easy Bake Ultimate Oven, Pink/Purple

text_fidelity_a: shoprotik Tarot Cards Deck for Beginners with Meanings On Them, Vintage Card with Guidebook … Definitely a great deck of cards for the beginner.  I am not a tarot reader, but a collector of the decks.  I do have a couple of the Rider-Waite cards that the illustrations on this set come from, but this is the first one I have seen with all the peripheral information (around the edges).  I think it adds quite a bit to the cards.  For people who like to have tarot readings, this set would allow them to assimilate a bit of their own ideas about what is meant by the cards that reveal themselves during their reading.  This deck also comes with a lovely little drawstring back which is a nice touch.  As I said, I have a small collection of tarot decks and most do not come with a bag to hold them and if they were bundled with a book on their own meanings of the cards, those decks don't even have a decent box unless you keep the entire, fairly large box that both the book and the deck came in.  I know that sounds stupid, but I have some beautiful decks that were sent in lovely packages that illustrate the deck inside and I even have an "art" set of tarot cards that are quite large - too large to shuffle easily -that came in a box similar to an old cigar box.  Yes, I really love collecting these tarot decks and this set is unique with all the information on each card plus using the Rider-Waite illustrations - they are bright, beautiful and "understandable" if you take my meaning.  Lovely deck for a very reasonable price.

The Schleich is well made and better than many toy dinosaurs out there, but when compared side-by-side you can really see the difference between the two. This is a throw-back to the old "SIMON" game that I played as a kid. You press the yellow button on her belt and her skirt lights up in different order and sequence. The purpose is to press the coordinating blue or red buttons on belt to match the order of the lights.  It has five levels of difficulty and music that plays when you press the buttons. text_fidelity_a:
Radio Flyer 6V Battery Powered Bumper Car, Electric Ride On with Remote, Toddler Ride On Toy for Ages 1.5+ Years Simply Excellent, you set the control amount, then place the young driver in.
Control amounts:
Parental - you have a remote control, and can drive your little speedster wherever you want to.
Youngster - your race car driver has full control over the vehicle
Mixed - should the little one be racing towards danger, you can override their controls and save the day.

The biggest problem with this is refraining from showing your young driver what it would atke to cause an airbag to deploy! (There are no airbags installed, and no children were hurt in the making of this review!)

The car is easy for young hands to control, and good fun! The remote is easy to operate. The car travels at the speed of a slow walk, yet the screams and giggles will make you think it is going a lot faster!

The battery lasts a long time, I didn't actually time a full charge to empty but noticed in all my (extensive) testing I had to recharge it only once.
Well made, easy to put together, a good 30 minutes though, so be prepared.

This will cause smiles and joy for a long time. Its really well thought out and built.

text_fidelity_a:
7 Wonders We're a game playing family. With 84 board/card games and counting, I feel like something of an expert on board games. This was an exceptionally good game. Unlike some strategy games, there doesn't seem to be any one strategy that's going to always work. You have to be flexible, depending upon which wonder you end up with, the cards you get, and the strategies your opponents are using. You have to pay particular attention to the strategies of your nearest neighbors on either side because many actions and many cards play off of them. No cards or actions play directly off of an opponent who is not your neighbor. That, too, is a nice feature. It's not that you shouldn't watch what the people across the table are doing, but it's more important to know what the guys to the right and left are doing. Especially when you're dealing with higher numbers of players, that makes it easier to keep up with. That's a big part of why it works as well for 7 players as it does for 3. That, and the fact that game play is simultaneous -- no turn taking! So there's very little down time and the games moves quickly.

The only reason I didn't give this game 5 stars is that the game comes with rules for a 2-player variation that I do not believe is very good. I was hoping that this would be a game I could play with my husband after our (young) kids went to bed, but after trying several times we both agreed on two things:

1) There are much better 2-player games.
2) This game is much better with 3-7 players.

For those reasons, we will only pull it out when we have friends over. But it really, really is a top-notch game for the right number of players. I mostly wrote this review to caution people who are considering buying it more for it's two-player extendability than anything else.
text_fidelity_b: 7 Wonders

Thames & Kosmos Ooze Labs Colorful Crystal Lab STEM Experiment Kit & Lab Setup | Awesome Geometric Crystals, Dazzling Displays, with 11 Shiny, Sparkly, Safe Experiments | Stickers to Decorate Your Lab These days with many kids doing home schooling due to lockdowns, this would be a great home schoolilng science project or lesson.

The age recommendation is for children six and up, however since most of these experiments require the use of a pot of boiling water, I think the manufacturer should increase the age requirement. Parental supervision is of course a great idea. The booklet is easy to understand, however it might be more difficult for younger children to read and understand the instructions.

I only tried the first experiment in the kit and it worked as expected, and it was the easiest, fastest experiment to get results. The instructions were easy to follow. (I also lacked any distilled water which many of the experiment recipes call for). It was fun for me as an adult to try.

I am not sure if this is an option or not, but it would be nice if refills on the "magic water, colors, (maybe even some not available in this kit) and paper cones) were made available so kids (or adults) can continue to keep playing and making different crystals. (Alum powder and food coloring are both readily available at any grocer.)

The box is attractively marked and would make a great gift for any adult or child who likes science or educational toys. This kit is compatible with other chemistry sets available from the same company.

All in all, it's a fun, educational kit that anyone can enjoy. The only true down side is that it may try the patience of kids who like instant results. Some of these experiments take two or three days to have decent crystals develop. I liked the kit and found it fascinating. I can't wait to try the other experiments in the kit.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Ooze Labs Colorful Crystal Lab STEM Experiment Kit & Lab Setup | Awesome Geometric Crystals, Dazzling Displays, with 11 Shiny, Sparkly, Safe Experiments | Stickers to Decorate Your Lab

text_fidelity_a: Force1 U45W FPV Drone with Camera for Adults - VR Ready Quadcopter RTF Remote Control Drone with 720p HD Wide Angle Drone Camera, 6 Axis Gyro, Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, and 2 Drone Batteries I was so excited to get this drone.  I have flown a pretty nice professional DJI but knew this would not be the same.  It arrived on time and in excellent shape.  First problem was there was only 2 batteries (supposed to be 3).  I charged the batteries (in the garbage charger).  I tried to charge them in my B6 charger but it ready low cell voltage- I should have known then there was an issue.  After assembling everything I took it out and followed the directions to calibrate and sync the drone.  It started up and rose up about 10 feet and started drifting to the right no matter what I did.  I landed it and recalibrated and had the same results.  Then the low battery beeping started.  I landed and changed out batteries (total flight time was less than 5 mins).  The second battery would not even turn on the lights.  Recharged the first battery and in 3 mins the drone crashed with a dead battery.  Charged the second battery again and no go.  So frustrated and disappointed.  I packed it all up and put in for a return.  There are a lot of websites that HIGHLY recommend this drone- I have a feeling they are paid for this as this thing is truly unusable.  The trim functions don't do a darn thing and the batteries are horrible.  Thanks to Amazon for a great hassle free return.
text_fidelity_b: Force1 U45W FPV Drone with Camera for Adults - VR Ready Quadcopter RTF Remote Control Drone with 720p HD Wide Angle Drone Camera, 6 Axis Gyro, Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, and 2 Drone Batteries

I hate to receive kits and cardboard boxes that just fall apart.

There are 437 plastic building pieces. That’s a lot of pieces. So of course you want to be careful not to lose any. Because you will not be able to perform all of the experiments year after year if you continue to lose pieces.

Though most everything is included, not everything is included. For example you’ll need some Neodymium magnets if you do not already have some.

The lesson plans are the same as the instruction manual. There are no worksheets and such with this kit.

The online videos are simply silent videos showing you the final product of each experiment. It would’ve been nice if the videos were more educational.

Kids do really like experiments like this. And overall it’s a nice kit, but certainly far from exceptional. I also think it’s a bit pricey for what it is.

Mountains Out of Molehills | Family Board Game for 2-4 Players | Two-Level Gameboard Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Great Gateway Game for Ages 9+ This is a good programmable movement game for 2 - 4 players. You draft a set of movement cards, then organize them into a plan of action for your turn, and you let your mole loose on the dirt. Everywhere you pass, you add to the pile of dirt until your dirt piles get so large that they topple over, which usually happens near the end of every game...

...but the real fun of this game is the rock. If your mole hits the rock, which moves around each round at the whim of the player who drafts the right card, then you bump, switch directions, and watch your plan fail and falter. It's funny, even for the person who gets messed up because of it.

So this is a very fun game that is light and easy to learn. I wish the underground was a little clearer in terms of where the spaces are, or that the moles were a little bit better sized for the pieces. It works though.

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola DigiTools Paint Pack Okay first off -- you can just download the app for this product in your Apple or Android app store. It will be somewhat limited, including having some of the "backgrounds" aka digital coloring pages disabled. There are more than one DigiTools apps - I was able to unlock two of the currently available four with this set: Their paint app and their airbrush app. Other sets that include different tools can unlock the other two (including a 3D set). The App consists of the backgrounds and several solid colored canvases. Using the appropriate tool allows you to do things like paint, stamp included images onto your scene, roll paint or images along your painting. Staying true to the Crayola kid friendly tradition the app doesn't include any sort of advanced features (no layers, etc). Your tools, an eraser, and an undo button are all you will find here.

The tools (what you're really buying here) consists of a Stamper, a roller, a brush, and an airbrush. Basically all of these (except the brush) are just several stylus nubs embedded into plastic tools that are kid friendly. The brush looks just like a run of the mill cheap brush (I can see kids grabbing it to paint with for real so look out for that) but when you hold it properly it too works like a stylus.

If you or the kids graduate out of the app and decide that say they do want to use them on more advanced programs? Good news and bad news there... The good news is that since these are basically just kid friendly tablet tools, yes these work in others apps. The bad news is that if you plan to say drag the stamper across your screen to get three lines at once? That's not going to happen. The screen will see this same as if you are using two fingers at once. So, for example, when I used these tools in Sketchbook pro? The brush worked perfectly. The airbrush and roller tools worked IF I tilted them so that only one nub was touching the screen at a time (otherwise it thought I was trying to pinch in and out / zoom). The stamper tool, which has three nubs, was basically useless.

The brush (the most useful tool in the pack) is also what makes this overall a 4 not a 5 star tool. The bristles are very fragile, I used this set a couple of times, put them away in the included carrying case, went to draw again and hmm the bristles were all fanned out and bent back. I don't know that the brush will hold up long term, it's already the most finicky tool in the set. Still, a fun kid friendly set that adults will love too.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola DigiTools Paint Pack
